extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, compliance officers, investor groups, and other SEC rulemaking stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final SEC rules and staff discussion governing climate-related disclosures (Regulation S-K subpart 1500 and related form instructions), including what emissions must be disclosed, timing, incorporation-by-reference, XBRL/interactive data requirements, phase-in dates, exemptions, and business-combination treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions not required
rubrics_metrics.description: As discussed in section II.H.3 above, the final rules will not require any registrant to disclose its Scope 3 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release reiterates that Scope 3 disclosures are not mandated by the final rules (see supra section II.H.3); commenters advocated various approaches but the Commission declined to require Scope 3 reporting in the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG emissions disclosure limited to Item 1505
rubrics_metrics.description: All registrants subject to the final rules, including SRCs and EGCs, are not required to disclose GHG emissions metrics other than as required by Item 1505, including where GHG emissions are included as part of a transition plan, target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1505 is the operative provision for required GHG emissions disclosure; other climate-related information (e.g., in transition plans or targets) does not impose separate GHG metrics obligations beyond Item 1505. The text also notes that registrants will disclose Scopes 1 and/or 2 in Form 10-Q only when they elect to do so pursuant to Item 1505, while foreign private issuers subject to the GHG requirement must provide emissions disclosure in their Form 20-F (though they may provide it on a delayed basis in an amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual timing of climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will generally require disclosures on an annual basis, which will allow investors to make better comparisons across time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission adopted annual reporting to address problems under voluntary regimes where companies often disclose sustainability data many months after the fiscal year (examples cited: Corporate Knights; letters from Morningstar and others noting one- to two-year delays). Annual timing is intended to improve comparability across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from Scopes 1 and 2 reporting for SRCs and EGCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules include an exemption from Scopes 1 and 2 emissions reporting for both SRCs and EGCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exemption is discussed in section II.H and informs differing applicability and compliance dates across filer types; related commentary and cross-references appear throughout the release (see e.g., infra section II.O for compliance dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference into Forms S-1, S-4, and S-11
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may incorporate by reference the climate-related disclosures required by the final rules to the extent they are permitted to do so under Forms S-1, S-4, and S-11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a registrant is eligible and elects to incorporate by reference, those forms require incorporation of the latest Form 10-K and all other Exchange Act reports filed since the end of the fiscal year covered by that Form 10-K (see Form S-1, General Instruction VII; Form S-1, Item 12; Form S-4, Items 11 and 13; Form S-11, Item 29). The release also explains a specific timing approach where prior-year emissions disclosure incorporated from a prior filing may satisfy Item 1505 obligations if (1) the registration statement becomes effective after filing its Form 10-K for the latest fiscal year but before filing a Form 10-K/A or the second-quarter Form 10-Q containing the prior year's emissions disclosure, and (2) the registrant discloses Item 1505 information in a Form 10-K/A or second-quarter Form 10-Q rather than in its Form 10-K (see Item 1505(c)(1)). Citations: 17 CFR 230.411 and 17 CFR 240.12b-23.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms S-3 and F-3 treatment and incorporation-date clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms S-3 and F-3 are not being amended to reference subpart 1500 because the required climate-related disclosures would be included in a registrant's Form 10-K or 20-F annual report that is incorporated by reference into those Securities Act registration statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release notes, however, that these forms are amended to clarify the date as of which disclosure required by Item 1505(a) must be incorporated. See Proposing Release, section J, note 690, and the discussion in section II.H.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate disclosures apply to business combination transactions and proxy/info statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules' subpart 1500 disclosure requirements apply to business combination transactions involving a securities offering registered on Forms S-4 and F-4 and also to certain business combination transactions requiring a proxy statement on Schedule 14A or an information statement on Schedule 14C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release cites 17 CFR 240.14a-101 (Item 14(c)(1) and 14(c)(2)) and 17 CFR 240.14c-101 (Item 1) requiring furnishing of the S-4/F-4 Part B/C information as applicable. Form S-4 General Instruction B.3 and Form F-4 General Instruction B.3 require that if the registrant is subject to reporting requirements of Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act, the information required by subpart 1500 must be provided with respect to the registrant (and analogous language applies for the company being acquired under General Instruction C.3). The release acknowledges commenter concerns (e.g., private targets may lack advanced climate disclosure) and resource burdens on acquirors to collect and assess emissions data consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive data / XBRL submission requirement (Item 1508 and Reg S‑T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1508 of Regulation S-K and Rule 405(b)(4)(vii) of Regulation S-T require disclosures filed pursuant to subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K to be submitted as an Interactive Data File.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because financial statements are already structured in Inline XBRL, no new regulatory text is necessary to structure the disclosures filed pursuant to Article 14 of Regulation S-X. See Rule 405(b)(1)(i) of Regulation S-T. The release references Rules 405, 406, and 408 of Regulation S-T and explains related tagging expectations and commenters' concerns about costs and meaningfulness of XBRL for emissions data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline XBRL tagging for Article 14 disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not alter the requirements for registrants to tag their financial statement disclosures in Inline XBRL. Accordingly, financial statement disclosures provided pursuant to new Article 14 of Regulation S-X will be required to be tagged in accordance with those requirements at the time they are first required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Rule 405(b)(1)(i) of Regulation S-T. The release records commenters both supporting and opposing tagging (e.g., XBRL US, Ceres supporting tagging; Alliance Resource arguing costs and limited usefulness given estimate differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 6‑K furnishing treatment for foreign issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 6-K's treatment as furnished for purposes of section 18 has existed since the Commission adopted the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release references the Periodic Report of Foreign Issuer, Release No. 34-8069 (Apr. 28, 1967). For foreign private issuers, the GHG emissions reporting requirement is satisfied in the annual report on Form 20-F, although some foreign issuers may provide such emissions disclosure on a delayed basis in an amendment; Form 6-K filings remain 'furnished' rather than 'filed' for section 18 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase‑in schedule and differing compliance dates by filer type
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopted different compliance dates for different types of filers and different disclosure categories (e.g., GHG emissions, financial metrics, targets), with commenters proposing various extensions or accelerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release records numerous comment letters recommending varied phase-in periods: requests for one-year extensions (HP, ICI, Microsoft, PwC), two-three year extensions (KPMG), three-five years (CEMEX, Williams Cos.), shorter phase-ins for non-LAF registrants (AGs of Cal. et al.), and other customized schedules (CAQ recommending phase-ins by type of disclosure and filer status). See infra section II.O.3 for detailed compliance date discussion. The release explains final adoption of phase-in timing and cross-references compliance date discussions elsewhere in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of less prescriptive requirements and materiality qualifier; expanded safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopted less prescriptive requirements and a materiality qualifier for several of the final rule provisions and adopted an expanded safe harbor provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release references changes from the Proposing Release (e.g., adoption of a materiality qualifier and expansion of safe harbor in section II.J). These adjustments reflect responses to commenter concerns about prescriptiveness and potential liability; see section II.J and related text for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of international standards and data comparability (commenter guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged the Commission to consider adopting international standards to ensure the highest possibility for data comparability across reporting regimes and international regulatory bodies (e.g., ISSB Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters from Data Foundation, Ceres, ISS ESG, and others recommended harmonization and consideration of international taxonomies and standards. The release records these comments and cross-references discussions about XBRL and taxonomy adoption (see letters cited at notes 2516–2518).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis baseline and rulemaking guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The economic consequences of proposed rules (potential costs and benefits including effects on efficiency, competition, and capital formation) should be measured against a baseline, which is the best assessment of how the world would look in the absence of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release cites SEC Staff Guidance on Economic Analysis in SEC Rulemaking (Mar. 16, 2012) and case law (Nasdaq v. SEC) explaining that the baseline typically does not include recently proposed actions. The Commission must consider investor protection as well as impacts on efficiency, competition, and capital formation per statutory directives (15 U.S.C. 77b(b); 17 U.S.C. 78c(f); 17 U.S.C. 78w(a)(2)). See sections IV.A–C for economic analyses and statutory considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to consider existing Regulation S‑K/S‑X guidance and applicable accounting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must consider how climate change issues may be required to be disclosed under existing rules (primarily Regulation S-K and Regulation S-X) and applicable accounting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release points to the 2010 Guidance (section III) for an overview and notes applicability of FASB ASC Topic 450 (Contingencies) and ASC Topic 275 (Risks and Uncertainties). It also references Securities Act Rule 408 and Exchange Act Rule 12b-20, which require disclosure of 'such further material information, if any, as may be necessary to make the required statements... not misleading.' Risk factor disclosure item shifts (Item 503(c) moved to Item 105) are also noted (see Release No. 33-10618).
